     2→name: Shopify App Stack Knowledge
     3→description: Accumulated patterns, lessons, and gotchas from building Shopify apps at Boldteq
     4→type: reference
     5→stack: shopify-app
     6→---
     7→
     8→## Stack
     9→Remix + TypeScript + Polaris + Prisma + PostgreSQL + Shopify Billing API
    10→
    11→## Projects Built On This Stack
    12→- Pinzo (ZIP code checker widget)
    13→- QuizSnap (product recommendation quizzes)
    14→- Size Chart & Recommender (AI size recommendations)
    15→
    16→## Critical Patterns
    17→
    18→### Auth
    19→- Always call `authenticate.admin(request)` at the top of every loader/action
    20→- Shop is always obtained from the authenticated session, never from query params
    21→- Storefront/public routes must validate Shopify origin or use signed requests
    22→
    23→### Database
    24→- Every Prisma query MUST include `shop: session.shop` in the where clause
    25→- Shops are onboarded with `upsert` to be idempotent — safe to call multiple times
    26→- Index: `shop`, `createdAt` (desc), and any field used in filters
    27→
    28→### Billing
    29→- Check subscription before rendering any paid feature in the loader
    30→- Webhook `APP_SUBSCRIPTIONS_UPDATE` → update local subscription status
    31→- Always offer a trial on first install (typically 7-14 days)
    32→
    33→### Webhooks
    34→- Validate HMAC before any processing — reject and return 401 if invalid
    35→- Always return 200 immediately — process async
    36→- Handle mandatory webhooks: `shop/redact`, `customers/redact`, `customers/data_request`
    37→
    38→### Storefront Widgets
    39→- No React, no framework — pure JS + CSS only
    40→- Load asynchronously to never block merchant storefront performance
    41→- Merchant config via `section.settings` schema in theme extension
    42→- Public API endpoints (`api.*` subdomain or `/api/public/`) — validate Shopify origin
    43→
    44→## Common Gotchas
    45→- Remix loaders run on every navigation — keep them fast, don't do heavy work in loaders
    46→- Polaris `IndexTable` requires `resourceName` and `itemCount` — easy to forget
    47→- `useFetcher` for mutations that shouldn't trigger full navigation
    48→- Session token expires — always handle 401 by redirecting to re-auth
    49→
    50→## Deployment
    51→- Vercel for standard apps
    52→- Railway when persistent server processes are needed (queues, background jobs)
    53→- Always set `SHOPIFY_APP_URL` env var correctly — wrong URL breaks OAuth

1→# Pinzo — Shopify App Project Brain
     2→
     3→## Stack (Exact Versions)
     4→- **Framework:** React Router 7 (`@shopify/shopify-app-react-router` v1) — NOT Remix
     5→- **UI:** Shopify Polaris v13 (`@shopify/polaris`) — use ONLY Polaris components, never raw HTML for layout
     6→- **App Bridge:** `@shopify/app-bridge-react` v4 — for all Shopify admin UI interactions
     7→- **Auth:** `shopify.server.ts` → `authenticate.admin(request)` — required before every Shopify API call
     8→- **Database:** Prisma v6 + SQLite (dev) / PostgreSQL (prod)
     9→- **Language:** TypeScript everywhere — zero plain `.js` files allowed
    10→- **Bundler:** Vite v6
    11→- **Node:** ≥20.19
    12→
    13→## Folder Structure
    14→```
    15→app/
    16→  routes/           ← All file-based routes
    17→  billing.server.ts ← Billing/subscription logic
    18→  db.server.ts      ← Prisma client singleton
    19→  plans.ts          ← Pricing plan definitions (Free/Pro/Ultimate)
    20→  shopify.server.ts ← Shopify auth + API setup
    21→  root.tsx          ← Root component
    22→  entry.server.tsx  ← Server entry
    23→prisma/
    24→  schema.prisma     ← Database schema
    25→  migrations/       ← Migration history
    26→.claude/
    27→  settings.json     ← Shared permissions config
    28→  commands/         ← Slash commands (/feature, /fix, /review)
    29→  agents/           ← Specialized agents (builder, bug-fixer)
    30→```
    31→
    32→## Database Models (Prisma)
    33→- **Session** — Shopify OAuth session storage (do NOT modify)
    34→- **ZipCode** — shop, zipCode, label, zone, message, eta, type (allowed/blocked)
    35→- **DeliveryRule** — shop, name, zone, zipCodes, minOrderAmount, deliveryFee, freeShippingAbove, estimatedDays, cutoffTime, daysOfWeek, priority
    36→- **WaitlistEntry** — shop, email, zipCode, note, status (waiting/notified/converted)
    37→- **WidgetConfig** — shop, position, colors, heading, placeholder, buttonText, messages, borderRadius, customCss
    38→- **Subscription** — shop, planId, billingInterval, shopifySubscriptionId, status, trialEndsAt
    39→
    40→## Route Patterns
    41→| Route Pattern | Purpose |
    42→|---|---|
    43→| `app._index.tsx` | Dashboard |
    44→| `app.*.tsx` | Admin pages (require authenticate.admin) |
    45→| `api.*.tsx` | Public API endpoints (storefront widget) |
    46→| `webhooks.*.tsx` | Webhook handlers |
    47→| `auth.*.tsx` | OAuth flow (do NOT modify) |
    48→
    49→## Architecture Rules
    50→1. **Auth first** — always call `authenticate.admin(request)` before any Shopify API usage
    51→2. **Loaders/actions only** — Shopify API calls ONLY inside loaders and actions, never inside components
    52→3. **Polaris only** — use ONLY Polaris v13 components for all UI inside `app.*` routes
    53→4. **Public APIs** — `api.*` routes serve the storefront widget (no auth required, return JSON)
    54→5. **Webhooks** — handle idempotently, return 200 quickly, no heavy processing inline
    55→6. **DB access** — import `db` from `~/db.server` for all Prisma operations
    56→7. **Billing** — use `billing.server.ts` for all subscription checks and plan changes
    57→8. **Plans** — reference `plans.ts` for plan IDs and feature flags
    58→
    59→## UI Rules (Polaris v13)
    60→- Layout: `Page`, `Layout`, `Layout.Section`, `Card`, `BlockStack`, `InlineStack`
    61→- Data: `DataTable`, `IndexTable`, `ResourceList`
    62→- Forms: `Form`, `FormLayout`, `TextField`, `Select`, `Checkbox`
    63→- Feedback: `Toast` for user-facing errors and success, `Banner` for persistent alerts
    64→- Loading: `SkeletonPage`, `SkeletonBodyText`, `SkeletonDisplayText` — always add loading states
    65→- Modals: `Modal` component with `active` prop
    66→- Navigation: use App Bridge `useNavigate` for in-app navigation
    67→
    68→## Code Rules
    69→- Fix ALL TypeScript errors before marking anything done — run `npm run typecheck`
    70→- Error handling on every async operation (try/catch in actions/loaders)
    71→- Never use raw `fetch()` for Shopify API — use the graphql client from `authenticate.admin()`
    72→- Before writing new code: read 2-3 existing similar route files and match their exact pattern
    73→- No `any` types — use proper TypeScript types or infer from Prisma
    74→- `useActionData`, `useLoaderData` for data in components — never fetch inside components
    75→
    76→## Commands
    77→```bash
    78→npm run dev          # Start dev server via Shopify CLI
    79→npm run build        # Build for production
    80→npm run typecheck    # TypeScript validation (run after every change)
    81→npm run lint         # ESLint check
    82→npm run setup        # Prisma generate + migrate (first time)
    83→npx prisma studio    # Visual DB browser
    84→npx prisma migrate dev --name <name>   # Create new migration
    85→npx shopify app deploy                  # Deploy to Shopify
    86→```
    87→
    88→## When Building a Feature — Always Follow This Order
    89→1. Read CLAUDE.md (this file) — understand rules
    90→2. Read 2-3 existing similar route files (e.g. `app.zip-codes.tsx`, `app.settings.tsx`)
    91→3. Build the route file: `loader` (fetch data) + `action` (handle mutations) + default export component
    92→4. Use only Polaris v13 for all UI
    93→5. Add error handling in action with try/catch, return errors via `json()`
    94→6. Add loading states with Polaris Skeleton components
    95→7. Run `npm run typecheck` — fix every error before finishing
    96→8. List all files created and what to test
    97→
    98→## Existing Feature Reference
    99→- ZIP code CRUD → `app/routes/app.zip-codes.tsx`
   100→- Delivery rules → `app/routes/app.delivery-rules.tsx`
   101→- Waitlist viewer → `app/routes/app.waitlist.tsx`
   102→- Widget config → `app/routes/app.widget.tsx`
   103→- Billing/pricing → `app/routes/app.pricing.tsx` + `app/billing.server.ts`
   104→- Settings → `app/routes/app.settings.tsx`
   105→- Public ZIP API → `app/routes/api.zip-check.tsx`
   106→- Public widget config API → `app/routes/api.widget-config.tsx`
   107→- Waitlist signup API → `app/routes/api.waitlist.tsx`

    11→## Projects Built On This Stack
    12→- Rankora (AI resume screening SaaS)

    14→## Critical Patterns
    15→
    16→### Auth (Supabase Auth)
    17→- `createServerClient` for server components and API routes — validates session server-side
    18→- `createBrowserClient` for client components only
    19→- Never use `supabase.auth.getSession()` on server — use `getUser()` which validates with Supabase servers
    20→- Protect routes in `middleware.ts` for broad protection, then check user in individual components for granular control
    21→
    22→### Database (Supabase + RLS)
    23→- RLS must be enabled on ALL tables from day one — `ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`
    24→- Default deny: no default policy = deny all. Add explicit policies.
    25→- Standard user-scoped policy: `USING (auth.uid() = user_id)`
    26→- Service role key stays server-side only — never in client code or `.env.local` committed to git
    27→- Use migrations for ALL schema changes — never use the Supabase dashboard editor for production schema
    28→
    29→### Billing (Stripe)
    30→- Create Stripe customer on signup, store `stripe_customer_id` on user record
    31→- Subscription status stored locally AND validated via webhook for reliability
    32→- Webhook endpoint: validate `stripe.webhooks.constructEvent()` signature first
    33→- Handle these webhooks minimum: `checkout.session.completed`, `customer.subscription.updated`, `customer.subscription.deleted`, `invoice.payment_failed`
    34→- Gate features in server components/API routes by checking local `subscription_status`
    35→
    36→### API Design
    37→- App Router API routes: one file per resource, GET/POST in same file
    38→- Always validate with Zod before touching the database
    39→- Return consistent error shapes: `{ error: string, code?: string }`
    40→- Rate limiting on public endpoints
    41→
    42→### File Structure

    44→app/
    45→  (auth)/login, signup, reset

    47→  api/ ← server-side API routes
    48→components/ui/ ← shadcn primitives
    49→lib/supabase/server.ts + client.ts
    50→lib/stripe.ts
    51→lib/validations/ ← Zod schemas
    52→```

    54→## Common Gotchas
    55→- Next.js App Router: `cookies()` is async in Next.js 15 — `await cookies()`
    56→- Supabase `createServerClient` needs to be called once per request, not module-level

     2→name: widget-specialist
     3→description: Use this agent for storefront widget development, public API endpoints (api.*), JavaScript widget code, widget config, and anything related to the customer-facing ZIP code checker widget
     4→model: sonnet
     5→---
     6→
     7→You are a specialist in Shopify storefront widget development, public API design, and the customer-facing experience for the Pinzo app. You understand Shopify's storefront ecosystem: theme app extensions, script tags, app blocks, CSP, CORS, and performance requirements.
     8→
     9→## Your Domain
    10→Everything the **customer** sees and interacts with on the storefront:
    11→- The ZIP code checker widget (embedded JS)
    12→- Public API endpoints that the widget calls
    13→- Widget configuration that merchants set in admin
    14→- Theme app extension / app block integration
    15→
    16→## Collaboration Protocol
    17→
    18→### When to hand off to other agents
    19→- **Builder**: If you need a new admin page or significant admin-side UI changes
    20→- **Bug-fixer**: If you hit auth issues, Prisma errors, or TypeScript errors you can't resolve quickly
    21→- **Review (command)**: After completing widget changes, recommend `/review`
    22→
    23→### When other agents hand off to you
    24→- Builder may create new API endpoints and hand off for widget integration
    25→- Bug-fixer may resolve API-level bugs and hand off for widget-side fixes
    26→
    27→### Coordination rules
    28→- Document API contracts clearly: URL, method, params, response shape, error responses
    29→- If you change an API response shape, flag it — the widget code depends on it
    30→- If you add new widget config fields, document them for builder (admin page needs updating)
    31→
    32→## Public API Endpoints (No Shopify Auth)
    33→
    34→These routes serve the storefront widget — they return JSON, NO `authenticate.admin`:
    35→- `api.zip-check.tsx` — checks if a ZIP code is allowed/blocked for a shop
    36→- `api.widget-config.tsx` — returns widget styling config for a shop
    37→- `api.waitlist.tsx` — adds customer email to waitlist for unsupported ZIP codes
    38→
    39→### API Route Pattern
    40→```tsx
    41→import { json, type LoaderFunctionArgs, type ActionFunctionArgs } from "@shopify/shopify-app-react-router";
    42→import db from "../db.server";
    43→
    44→// CORS headers for storefront requests
    45→const corsHeaders = {
    46→  "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
    47→  "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "GET, POST, OPTIONS",
    48→  "Access-Control-Allow-Headers": "Content-Type",
    49→};
    50→
    51→// Handle preflight requests
    52→export async function loader({ request }: LoaderFunctionArgs) {
    53→  if (request.method === "OPTIONS") {
    54→    return new Response(null, { status: 204, headers: corsHeaders });
    55→  }
    56→
    57→  const url = new URL(request.url);
    58→  const shop = url.searchParams.get("shop");
    59→
    60→  if (!shop) {
    61→    return json({ error: "shop parameter required" }, { status: 400, headers: corsHeaders });
    62→  }
    63→
    64→  // Validate shop parameter format (prevent injection)
    65→  if (!/^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-]*\.myshopify\.com$/.test(shop)) {
    66→    return json({ error: "Invalid shop parameter" }, { status: 400, headers: corsHeaders });
    67→  }
    68→
    69→  const config = await db.widgetConfig.findUnique({ where: { shop } });
    70→  return json({ config }, { headers: corsHeaders });
    71→}
    72→```
    73→
    74→## Security for Public APIs
    75→- **Always validate `shop` parameter** — format must match `*.myshopify.com`
    76→- **Never expose** session tokens, API keys, or internal IDs in responses
    77→- **CORS headers** — storefront requests come from the merchant's domain, need `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`
    78→- **Rate limiting awareness** — these endpoints are called by every storefront visitor
    79→- **Input sanitization** — validate ZIP code format, email format, sanitize all user input
    80→- **CSP compliance** — widget JS must work within Shopify's Content Security Policy
    81→
    82→### Input Validation Patterns
    83→```tsx
    84→// ZIP code validation
    85→const zipCode = formData.get("zipCode")?.toString().trim();
    86→if (!zipCode || !/^[0-9]{5,6}$/.test(zipCode)) {
    87→  return json({ error: "Invalid ZIP code format" }, { status: 400, headers: corsHeaders });
    88→}
    89→
    90→// Email validation
    91→const email = formData.get("email")?.toString().trim().toLowerCase();
    92→if (!email || !/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(email)) {
    93→  return json({ error: "Invalid email format" }, { status: 400, headers: corsHeaders });
    94→}
    95→```
    96→
    97→## Widget Config (WidgetConfig model)
    98→Fields: `position`, `primaryColor`, `successColor`, `errorColor`, `backgroundColor`, `textColor`, `heading`, `placeholder`, `buttonText`, custom messages, `borderRadius`, `customCss`
    99→
   100→### Default styling principles
   101→- Match Shopify Dawn theme conventions
   102→- Responsive by default — works on mobile, tablet, desktop
   103→- Accessible — proper contrast ratios, focus states, aria labels
   104→- Non-intrusive — doesn't break the merchant's theme layout
   105→
   106→## ZIP Check Logic (ZipCode model)
   107→- `type: "allowed"` → show success message + delivery info from DeliveryRule
   108→- `type: "blocked"` → show error message + offer waitlist signup
   109→- No record found → treat as blocked (default deny)
   110→- Check DeliveryRules for zone-based messaging (fee, ETA, cutoff time)
   111→
   112→### Response Shapes (API Contract)
   113→
   114→#### GET /api/zip-check?shop=xxx&zipCode=12345
   115→```json
   116→// Success (ZIP allowed)
   117→{
   118→  "available": true,
   119→  "message": "Delivery available to your area!",
   120→  "zipCode": { "zipCode": "12345", "label": "Downtown", "zone": "A", "eta": "1-2 days" },
   121→  "deliveryRule": { "deliveryFee": 5.99, "freeShippingAbove": 50, "estimatedDays": 2 }
   122→}
   123→
   124→// Failure (ZIP blocked or not found)
   125→{
   126→  "available": false,
   127→  "message": "Sorry, we don't deliver to this area yet.",
   128→  "waitlistEnabled": true
   129→}
   130→```
   131→
   132→#### GET /api/widget-config?shop=xxx
   133→```json
   134→{
   135→  "config": {
   136→    "position": "bottom-right",
   137→    "primaryColor": "#000000",
   138→    "heading": "Check Delivery Availability",
   139→    "placeholder": "Enter your ZIP code",
   140→    "buttonText": "Check",
   141→    ...
   142→  }
   143→}
   144→```
   145→
   146→#### POST /api/waitlist (body: shop, email, zipCode)
   147→```json
   148→// Success
   149→{ "success": true, "message": "You've been added to our waitlist!" }
   150→
   151→// Already on waitlist
   152→{ "success": true, "message": "You're already on our waitlist." }
   153→
   154→// Error
   155→{ "error": "Invalid email format" }
   156→```
   157→
   158→## Widget Admin Page
   159→`app/routes/app.widget.tsx` — the admin page where merchants configure widget styling:
   160→- Changes update `WidgetConfig` in DB
   161→- Widget reads this config via `api.widget-config.tsx`
   162→- Live preview should show changes in real-time before saving
   163→- Preview should show all states: default, loading, success, error, waitlist
   164→
   165→## Shopify Storefront Integration Patterns
   166→
   167→### App Blocks (Preferred — Online Store 2.0)
   168→Theme app extensions with app blocks are the modern approach:
   169→- Merchant adds the block via theme editor
   170→- No code injection needed
   171→- Works with all OS 2.0 themes
   172→- Block renders the widget container, loads the widget JS
   173→
   174→### Script Tags (Legacy fallback)
   175→For non-OS 2.0 themes:
   176→- Injected via Shopify ScriptTag API
   177→- Must be lightweight — minimize bundle size
   178→- Must handle being loaded asynchronously
   179→- Must not conflict with theme JS
   180→
   181→### Performance Requirements
   182→- Widget JS bundle: target < 15KB gzipped
   183→- First paint: < 100ms after script load
   184→- API response time: aim for < 200ms
   185→- Lazy load non-critical features (waitlist form)
   186→- Cache widget config on the client (localStorage with TTL)
   187→
   188→## Widget JavaScript Best Practices
   189→```javascript
   190→// Self-contained — no global namespace pollution
   191→(function() {
   192→  const WIDGET_VERSION = '1.0';
   193→  const API_BASE = '{{APP_URL}}';
   194→  const CACHE_TTL = 5 * 60 * 1000; // 5 minutes
   195→
   196→  // Cache config in localStorage
   197→  function getCachedConfig(shop) {
   198→    const cached = localStorage.getItem(`zcc_config_${shop}`);
   199→    if (cached) {
   200→      const { data, timestamp } = JSON.parse(cached);
   201→      if (Date.now() - timestamp < CACHE_TTL) return data;
   202→    }
   203→    return null;
   204→  }
   205→
   206→  // Accessible widget structure
   207→  function createWidget(config) {
   208→    const widget = document.createElement('div');
   209→    widget.setAttribute('role', 'form');
   210→    widget.setAttribute('aria-label', config.heading || 'Check delivery availability');
   211→    // ... build widget DOM
   212→    return widget;
   213→  }
   214→})();
   215→```
   216→
   217→## Accessibility Requirements
   218→- All form inputs must have associated labels
   219→- Color contrast must meet WCAG 2.1 AA (4.5:1 for text)
   220→- Focus management — focus moves logically through the widget
   221→- Screen reader announcements for results (success/error)
   222→- Keyboard navigation — all interactions possible without mouse
   223→- `aria-live="polite"` for dynamic result messages
   224→
   225→## Self-Validation Checklist
   226→1. CORS headers present on ALL public API responses (including errors)
   227→2. Shop parameter validated on every API endpoint
   228→3. Input sanitization for ZIP codes, emails, all user input
   229→4. No `authenticate.admin` in `api.*` routes
   230→5. API response shapes match the documented contract above
   231→6. Widget config defaults exist for every field (never undefined)
   232→7. Run `npm run typecheck` — zero errors
   233→

    32→5. Run `npx prisma generate` (to update TypeScript types)
    33→6. Update any route files that reference changed models

    36→### For Query Optimization
    37→1. Check existing queries in route files
    38→2. Add indexes for frequently queried fields
    39→3. Use `select` to fetch only needed fields (not full records)
    40→4. Use `include` sparingly — avoid N+1 queries
    41→5. Use `db.$transaction()` for multi-step operations

    43→### For Data Operations
    44→1. Always include `where: { shop: session.shop }` for security
    45→2. Use `upsert` for singleton records (WidgetConfig, Subscription)
    46→3. Use `createMany` for bulk inserts (ZIP code imports)
    47→4. Use `deleteMany` for bulk deletes with proper `where` clause
    48→5. Use transactions for multi-step operations: `db.$transaction([...])`

    50→### Query Patterns

    52→// Singleton upsert (WidgetConfig, Subscription)
    53→await db.widgetConfig.upsert({
    54→  where: { shop: session.shop },
    55→  update: { ...configData },
    56→  create: { shop: session.shop, ...configData },
    57→});
    58→
    59→// Paginated list
    60→const [items, total] = await db.$transaction([
    61→  db.zipCode.findMany({
    62→    where: { shop: session.shop },
    63→    skip: (page - 1) * pageSize,
    64→    take: pageSize,
    65→    orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" },
    66→  }),
    67→  db.zipCode.count({ where: { shop: session.shop } }),
    68→]);
